title: Pseudomonads and Descent
extended_summary:
This document is a PhD thesis in mathematics, not an education or AI-in-writing study. The thesis addresses theoretical problems in 2-dimensional category theory, especially the study of pseudomonads and descent objects, with applications to descent theory, weighted bilimits, coherence, and presentations of categorical structures. It is organized as an introductory chapter plus four single-authored papers produced during the author's doctoral studies.

The approach is entirely mathematical and conceptual. Across its chapters, the thesis develops formal results on pseudomonadic pseudofunctors, pseudo-Kan extensions, bilimits, biadjoint triangle theorems, lifting of biadjoints, lax algebras, and related categorical constructions. It also includes work on freely generated n-categories, coinserters, computads, and links between categorical presentations and topology. The text presents definitions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs rather than any educational intervention, classroom implementation, or learner-facing technology.

The population implicitly represented is the doctoral researcher/author within a university PhD program, but there is no empirical participant sample and no education-study context involving secondary students, teachers, or schools. The institutional context named is the UC|UP Joint PhD Program in Mathematics, with support from research centers and funding bodies in Portugal and Brazil, but these are acknowledgements rather than study sites.

The main conclusion is that the thesis contributes new theoretical results in category theory, especially concerning pseudomonads, descent theory, coherence, and presentations of categorical structures.
